raw: Act 3, Scene 5 — An open Gallery to Juliet’s Chamber, overlooking the Garden

sentences.en: An open Gallery to Juliet’s Chamber, overlooking the Garden
sentences.ko: 정원이 내려다보이는 줄리엣 방의 발코니

summary.en: Romeo and Juliet part at dawn. Then her parents tell her she must marry Paris. When she refuses, her father is furious.
summary.ko: 로미오와 줄리엣은 새벽에 헤어진다. 부모는 줄리엣에게 패리스와 결혼해야 한다고 말한다. 줄리엣이 거절하자 아버지는 크게 화를 낸다.

raw: Enter Romeo and Juliet.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Wilt thou be gone? It is not yet near day.
It was the nightingale, and not the lark,
That pierc’d the fearful hollow of thine ear;
Nightly she sings on yond pomegranate tree.
Believe me, love, it was the nightingale.

sentences.en: Will you leave?
sentences.ko: 떠나실 건가요?

sentences.en: It is not near day yet.
sentences.ko: 아직 날이 밝지 않았어요.

sentences.en: It was the nightingale, and not the lark, that entered your fearful ear.
sentences.ko: 당신의 겁먹은 귀에 들린 건 나이팅게일이지, 종다리가 아니에요.

sentences.en: She sings every night on that pomegranate tree over there.
sentences.ko: 그 새는 밤마다 저기 석류나무에서 노래해요.

sentences.en: Believe me, love, it was the nightingale.
sentences.ko: 믿어요, 내 사랑, 그건 나이팅게일이었어요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
It was the lark, the herald of the morn,
No nightingale. Look, love, what envious streaks
Do lace the severing clouds in yonder east.
Night’s candles are burnt out, and jocund day
Stands tiptoe on the misty mountain tops.
I must be gone and live, or stay and die.

sentences.en: It was the lark, the herald of the morning, not a nightingale.
sentences.ko: 나이팅게일이 아니라 아침을 알리는 종다리였어요.

sentences.en: Look, love, at the spiteful streaks of light breaking through the clouds in the east.
sentences.ko: 봐요, 내 사랑, 동쪽 구름 사이로 심술궂게 번지는 저 빛줄기를요.

sentences.en: The candles of night are burned out.
sentences.ko: 밤의 촛불은 이미 꺼졌어요.

sentences.en: And the happy day stands on tiptoe on the misty mountain tops.
sentences.ko: 그리고 행복한 하루가 안개 낀 산봉우리 위에서 발돋움하고 있어요.

sentences.en: I must leave and live, or stay and die.
sentences.ko: 떠나서 살거나, 아니면 남아서 죽어야 해요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Yond light is not daylight, I know it, I.
It is some meteor that the sun exhales
To be to thee this night a torchbearer
And light thee on thy way to Mantua.
Therefore stay yet, thou need’st not to be gone.

sentences.en: That light is not daylight, I know it.
sentences.ko: 저 빛은 낮의 빛이 아니라는 걸 알아요.

sentences.en: It is some meteor that the sun breathes out.
sentences.ko: 그건 태양이 내뿜는 유성일 뿐이에요.

sentences.en: It will be a torch for you tonight.
sentences.ko: 그것은 오늘 밤 당신을 위한 횃불이 될 거예요.

sentences.en: It will light your way to Mantua.
sentences.ko: 당신이 만토바로 가는 길을 비춰줄 거예요.

sentences.en: Therefore stay now. You do not need to leave.
sentences.ko: 그러니 지금은 머무세요. 떠날 필요 없어요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Let me be ta’en, let me be put to death,
I am content, so thou wilt have it so.
I’ll say yon grey is not the morning’s eye,
’Tis but the pale reflex of Cynthia’s brow.
Nor that is not the lark whose notes do beat
The vaulty heaven so high above our heads.
I have more care to stay than will to go.
Come, death, and welcome. Juliet wills it so.
How is’t, my soul? Let’s talk. It is not day.

sentences.en: Let me be caught. Let me be put to death.
sentences.ko: 차라리 붙잡히는 게 낫겠어요. 차라리 죽임을 당하겠어요.

sentences.en: I am content, if you want it that way.
sentences.ko: 당신이 원하신다면 그렇게 하겠어요.

sentences.en: I will say that gray light is not the morning's eye.
sentences.ko: 저 회색빛은 아침의 눈이 아니라고 말할게요.

sentences.en: It is only the pale light of Cynthia, the moon goddess.
sentences.ko: 그건 단지 달의 여신, 신시아의 창백한 빛일 뿐이에요.

sentences.en: That is not the lark whose notes beat the high vault of heaven above our heads.
sentences.ko: 우리 머리 위 높은 하늘을 울리는 건 종다리의 노래가 아니에요.

sentences.en: I want to stay more than I want to go.
sentences.ko: 떠나고 싶은 것보다 더 머물고 싶어요.

sentences.en: Come, death, and welcome me. Juliet wants it so.
sentences.ko: 죽음아 오라, 나를 데려가라. 줄리엣이 원하니까요.

sentences.en: How are you, my soul? Let's talk.
sentences.ko: 내 영혼, 기분이 어때요? 우리 이야기해요.

sentences.en: It is not day.
sentences.ko: 아직 낮이 아니에요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
It is, it is! Hie hence, be gone, away.
It is the lark that sings so out of tune,
Straining harsh discords and unpleasing sharps.
Some say the lark makes sweet division;
This doth not so, for she divideth us.
Some say the lark and loathed toad change eyes.
O, now I would they had chang’d voices too,
Since arm from arm that voice doth us affray,
Hunting thee hence with hunt’s-up to the day.
O now be gone, more light and light it grows.

sentences.en: It is, it is!
sentences.ko: 맞아요, 맞아요!

sentences.en: Hurry away! Go now!
sentences.ko: 어서 가세요! 지금 당장요!

sentences.en: It is the lark that sings out of tune.
sentences.ko: 음치처럼 노래하는 건 종다리예요.

sentences.en: It makes harsh sounds and unpleasant notes.
sentences.ko: 그건 거칠고 불쾌한 소리를 내죠.

sentences.en: Some say the lark makes sweet music.
sentences.ko: 어떤 이들은 종다리가 감미로운 음악을 만든다고 해요.

sentences.en: This one does not, because she divides us.
sentences.ko: 하지만 이 새는 우리를 갈라놓으니 그런 소리를 내지 않아요.

sentences.en: Some say the lark and the ugly toad swapped eyes.
sentences.ko: 어떤 이들은 종다리와 못생긴 두꺼비가 눈을 바꿨다고들 하죠.

sentences.en: Oh, I wish they had changed voices too.
sentences.ko: 오, 그들이 목소리도 바꾸었으면 좋았을 텐데.

sentences.en: That voice frightens us out of each other's arms.
sentences.ko: 그 목소리가 우리를 서로의 품에서 떼어놓네요.

sentences.en: It chases you away with a morning wake-up song.
sentences.ko: 아침을 깨우는 노래로 당신을 쫓아내요.

sentences.en: Now go. The light is growing more and more.
sentences.ko: 이제 가세요. 빛이 점점 더 밝아지고 있어요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: More light and light, more dark and dark our woes.

sentences.en: The lighter it gets, the darker our sorrows become.
sentences.ko: 빛이 밝아질수록 우리의 슬픔은 더 깊어지네요.

raw: Enter Nurse.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Madam.

sentences.en: Madam.
sentences.ko: 아가씨.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Nurse?

sentences.en: Nurse?
sentences.ko: 유모?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Your lady mother is coming to your chamber.
The day is broke, be wary, look about.

sentences.en: Your mother is coming to your room.
sentences.ko: 아가씨, 어머님이 방으로 오고 계셔.

sentences.en: The day has started.
sentences.ko: 날이 밝았어.

sentences.en: Be careful and look around.
sentences.ko: 조심하고 잘 살펴.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Then, window, let day in, and let life out.

sentences.en: Then, window, let the day in.
sentences.ko: 그럼 창문아, 햇빛은 들이고

sentences.en: Let life go out.
sentences.ko: 내 생명은 내보내라.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Farewell, farewell, one kiss, and I’ll descend.

sentences.en: Goodbye, goodbye.
sentences.ko: 잘 있어요, 잘 있어요.

sentences.en: One kiss, and I will climb down.
sentences.ko: 키스 한 번만, 그러고 내려갈게요.

raw: Descends.

sentences.en: Romeo climbs down.
sentences.ko: 로미오가 아래로 내려온다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Art thou gone so? Love, lord, ay husband, friend,
I must hear from thee every day in the hour,
For in a minute there are many days.
O, by this count I shall be much in years
Ere I again behold my Romeo.

sentences.en: Are you gone so soon?
sentences.ko: 벌써 가시는 건가요?

sentences.en: My love, my lord, my husband, and my friend, I must hear from you every hour of every day.
sentences.ko: 내 사랑, 내 주인, 내 남편, 내 친구, 매일 매시간 당신 소식을 들어야 해요.

sentences.en: Every minute apart will feel like many days.
sentences.ko: 떨어져 있는 매 분이 마치 며칠처럼 느껴질 거예요.

sentences.en: By this count, I will be much older before I see my Romeo again.
sentences.ko: 이렇게 세다가는, 로미오를 다시 볼 때쯤 나는 할머니가 되겠어요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Farewell!
I will omit no opportunity
That may convey my greetings, love, to thee.

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.ko: 잘 있어요!

sentences.en: I will not miss any chance to send my greetings and my love to you.
sentences.ko: 당신에게 안부와 내 사랑을 전할 기회를 절대 놓치지 않을게요.

speaker: JULIET
raw: O thinkest thou we shall ever meet again?

sentences.en: Do you think we will ever meet again?
sentences.ko: 우리가 다시 만날 수 있을 거라고 생각하시나요?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I doubt it not, and all these woes shall serve
For sweet discourses in our time to come.

sentences.en: I do not doubt it.
sentences.ko: 의심하지 않아요.

sentences.en: All these sorrows will serve as sweet stories for us to tell in the future.
sentences.ko: 이 모든 슬픔은 나중에 우리가 들려줄 달콤한 이야기가 될 거예요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O God! I have an ill-divining soul!
Methinks I see thee, now thou art so low,
As one dead in the bottom of a tomb.
Either my eyesight fails, or thou look’st pale.

sentences.en: Oh God!
sentences.ko: 오, 신이시여!

sentences.en: I have a soul that predicts bad things.
sentences.ko: 제 영혼은 불길한 일을 예감하곤 해요.

sentences.en: Now that you are down there, you look like someone dead at the bottom of a tomb.
sentences.ko: 당신이 저 아래에 있으니, 마치 무덤 바닥에 있는 죽은 사람처럼 보여요.

sentences.en: Either my eyesight is failing, or you look pale.
sentences.ko: 제 시력이 나빠진 건지, 아니면 당신의 얼굴이 창백해 보이는 건지 모르겠어요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
And trust me, love, in my eye so do you.
Dry sorrow drinks our blood. Adieu, adieu.

sentences.en: Trust me, love.
sentences.ko: 믿어줘요, 내 사랑.

sentences.en: You look that way in my eyes too.
sentences.ko: 내 눈에도 그렇게 보여요.

sentences.en: Dry sorrow drinks our blood.
sentences.ko: 메마른 슬픔이 우리의 피를 마시고 있어요.

sentences.en: Goodbye, goodbye.
sentences.ko: 잘 있어요, 잘 있어요.

raw: Exit below.

sentences.en: Romeo goes down and away.
sentences.ko: 로미오는 내려가서 멀어진다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O Fortune, Fortune! All men call thee fickle,
If thou art fickle, what dost thou with him
That is renown’d for faith? Be fickle, Fortune;
For then, I hope thou wilt not keep him long
But send him back.

sentences.en: Oh Fortune, Fortune!
sentences.ko: 아, 운명이여, 운명이여!

sentences.en: All men call you fickle.
sentences.ko: 모두들 너를 변덕쟁이라 부른다.

sentences.en: If you are fickle, why would you bother with him, when he is known for being faithful?
sentences.ko: 네가 변덕스럽다면, 성실하기로 이름난 그이와 무슨 볼일이 있겠느냐?

sentences.en: Be fickle, Fortune.
sentences.ko: 변덕을 부려라, 운명이여.

sentences.en: Then, I hope you will not keep him long.
sentences.ko: 그러면 그이를 오래 붙잡아 두지 않겠지.

sentences.en: I hope you send him back.
sentences.ko: 곧 돌려보내 주겠지.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Ho, daughter, are you up?

sentences.en: Hey, daughter, are you awake?
sentences.ko: 얘야, 깨어 있느냐?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Who is’t that calls? Is it my lady mother?
Is she not down so late, or up so early?
What unaccustom’d cause procures her hither?

sentences.en: Who is calling?
sentences.ko: 누가 부르지?

sentences.en: Is it my lady mother?
sentences.ko: 어머니신가?

sentences.en: Has she not gone to bed yet, or is she up so early?
sentences.ko: 아직 안 주무셨나, 아니면 이렇게 일찍 일어나셨나?

sentences.en: What unusual reason brings her here?
sentences.ko: 무슨 일로 여기 오시는 걸까?

raw: Enter Lady Capulet.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Why, how now, Juliet?

sentences.en: What is the matter, Juliet?
sentences.ko: 무슨 일이냐, 줄리엣?

speaker: JULIET
raw: Madam, I am not well.

sentences.en: Madam, I am not well.
sentences.ko: 어머니, 몸이 안 좋아요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Evermore weeping for your cousin’s death?
What, wilt thou wash him from his grave with tears?
And if thou couldst, thou couldst not make him live.
Therefore have done: some grief shows much of love,
But much of grief shows still some want of wit.

sentences.en: Are you still crying for your cousin's death?
sentences.ko: 아직도 사촌의 죽음을 슬퍼하며 울고 있니?

sentences.en: Will you wash him from his grave with your tears?
sentences.ko: 눈물로 그를 무덤에서 씻어낼 수라도 있겠니?

sentences.en: Even if you could, you could not make him live.
sentences.ko: 그럴 수 있다 해도, 그를 다시 살려낼 수는 없어.

sentences.en: Stop now.
sentences.ko: 이제 그만해라.

sentences.en: Some grief shows a lot of love.
sentences.ko: 슬픔이 깊은 건 사랑이 크다는 뜻일 수도 있지만,

sentences.en: But too much grief shows a lack of sense.
sentences.ko: 지나친 슬픔은 분별력이 없다는 걸 보여줄 뿐이야.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Yet let me weep for such a feeling loss.

sentences.en: Still, let me cry for such a great loss.
sentences.ko: 그래도 이런 큰 상실을 겪었으니 울게 해주세요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
So shall you feel the loss, but not the friend
Which you weep for.

sentences.en: That way you will feel the loss, but not bring back the friend you cry for.
sentences.ko: 그렇게 하면 네 슬픔만 달랠 뿐, 네가 우는 그 친구를 되살릴 수는 없어.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Feeling so the loss,
I cannot choose but ever weep the friend.

sentences.en: Because I feel this loss, I cannot help but always cry for my friend.
sentences.ko: 이런 상실감을 느끼고 있기에, 친구를 위해 계속 울 수밖에 없어요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Well, girl, thou weep’st not so much for his death
As that the villain lives which slaughter’d him.

sentences.en: Well, girl, you do not cry so much for his death.
sentences.ko: 얘야, 너는 그 애 죽음 때문에 우는 게 아니라

sentences.en: You cry because the villain who killed him is still alive.
sentences.ko: 그를 죽인 악당이 아직 살아있기 때문에 우는 것이지.

speaker: JULIET
raw: What villain, madam?

sentences.en: What villain, madam?
sentences.ko: 어머니, 어떤 악당 말씀이세요?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: That same villain Romeo.

sentences.en: That same villain, Romeo.
sentences.ko: 바로 그 악당, 로미오 말이야.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Villain and he be many miles asunder.
God pardon him. I do, with all my heart.
And yet no man like he doth grieve my heart.

sentences.en: 'Villain' and he are many miles apart.
sentences.ko: '악당'이라는 말과 그는 아주 멀리 떨어져 있어요.

sentences.en: God forgive him.
sentences.ko: 하나님, 그를 용서하소서.

sentences.en: I forgive him with all my heart.
sentences.ko: 저는 온 마음으로 그를 용서해요.

sentences.en: And yet no man hurts my heart like he does.
sentences.ko: 그런데도 그이만큼 제 마음을 아프게 하는 남자는 없어요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: That is because the traitor murderer lives.

sentences.en: That is because the traitor and murderer is still alive.
sentences.ko: 그건 배신자이자 살인마가 아직 살아있기 때문이야.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Ay madam, from the reach of these my hands.
Would none but I might venge my cousin’s death.

sentences.en: Yes, madam, far from the reach of my hands.
sentences.ko: 네, 어머니, 제 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 있죠.

sentences.en: I wish no one but me could take revenge for my cousin's death.
sentences.ko: 제 사촌의 원수는 저 말고는 아무도 갚지 않았으면 좋겠어요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
We will have vengeance for it, fear thou not.
Then weep no more. I’ll send to one in Mantua,
Where that same banish’d runagate doth live,
Shall give him such an unaccustom’d dram
That he shall soon keep Tybalt company:
And then I hope thou wilt be satisfied.

sentences.en: We will have revenge for it. Do not fear.
sentences.ko: 우리가 복수할 거다. 걱정 마라.

sentences.en: Stop crying now.
sentences.ko: 이제 그만 울어라.

sentences.en: I will send a message to someone in Mantua.
sentences.ko: 만토바에 있는 사람에게 메시지를 보낼 것이다.

sentences.en: That banished criminal lives there.
sentences.ko: 그 추방된 범죄자가 거기 살고 있어.

sentences.en: Someone there will give him a strong dose of poison.
sentences.ko: 그곳 누군가가 그에게 독약을 먹일 거다.

sentences.en: It will make him join Tybalt in death soon.
sentences.ko: 그러면 그는 곧 죽음으로 티볼트와 합류하게 될 거다.

sentences.en: Then I hope you will be satisfied.
sentences.ko: 그럼 네가 만족할 수 있을 거다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Indeed I never shall be satisfied
With Romeo till I behold him—dead—
Is my poor heart so for a kinsman vex’d.
Madam, if you could find out but a man
To bear a poison, I would temper it,
That Romeo should upon receipt thereof,
Soon sleep in quiet. O, how my heart abhors
To hear him nam’d, and cannot come to him,
To wreak the love I bore my cousin
Upon his body that hath slaughter’d him.

sentences.en: No, I will never be satisfied with Romeo until I see him—
sentences.ko: 아니요, 로미오를 볼 때까지는 절대 만족 못 해요—

sentences.en: Dead is my poor heart, so hurt for a relative.
sentences.ko: 죽어 있는 건 제 가여운 마음이에요. 친척 때문에 이토록 아프니까요.

sentences.en: Madam, if you could find just one man to carry a poison, I would mix it.
sentences.ko: 어머니, 독약을 가져갈 사람만 찾아 주시면, 제가 그 약을 타 드릴게요.

sentences.en: Then Romeo would soon sleep in peace after he received it.
sentences.ko: 그러면 로미오는 그걸 받고 곧 편히 잠들 거예요.

sentences.en: Oh, how much I hate to hear his name.
sentences.ko: 오, 그의 이름이 나오는 게 너무 싫어요.

sentences.en: I cannot reach him.
sentences.ko: 그에게 닿을 수 없어요.

sentences.en: I want to take my love for my cousin out on his body.
sentences.ko: 사촌에 대한 제 사랑을 그의 몸에 쏟아붓고 싶어요.

sentences.en: He is the one who killed him.
sentences.ko: 그이가 제 사촌을 죽였으니까요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Find thou the means, and I’ll find such a man.
But now I’ll tell thee joyful tidings, girl.

sentences.en: If you find a way, I will find such a man.
sentences.ko: 방법을 찾는다면, 그런 사람을 찾아내마.

sentences.en: But now I have happy news for you, girl.
sentences.ko: 하지만 이제 너에게 기쁜 소식을 전해주마.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
And joy comes well in such a needy time.
What are they, I beseech your ladyship?

sentences.en: Joy comes at a good time during such a sad time.
sentences.ko: 이렇게 괴로울 때 기쁜 소식이라니 반갑네요.

sentences.en: What is the news, I beg of your ladyship?
sentences.ko: 어머니, 무슨 소식인지 말씀해 주세요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Well, well, thou hast a careful father, child;
One who to put thee from thy heaviness,
Hath sorted out a sudden day of joy,
That thou expects not, nor I look’d not for.

sentences.en: Well, you have a very caring father, child.
sentences.ko: 얘야, 네 아버님은 참 자상한 분이시다.

sentences.en: He has planned a sudden day of joy to cheer you up.
sentences.ko: 너를 슬픔에서 건지려고 뜻밖의 기쁜 날을 정하셨단다.

sentences.en: You did not expect it, and I did not expect it either.
sentences.ko: 너도 예상 못 했고, 나도 예상치 못했어.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Madam, in happy time, what day is that?

sentences.en: Madam, how lucky!
sentences.ko: 어머니, 마침 잘됐네요!

sentences.en: What day is that?
sentences.ko: 그게 무슨 날인가요?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Marry, my child, early next Thursday morn
The gallant, young, and noble gentleman,
The County Paris, at Saint Peter’s Church,
Shall happily make thee there a joyful bride.

sentences.en: Well, my child.
sentences.ko: 그래, 얘야.

sentences.en: Early next Thursday morning, you will marry the brave and noble young Count Paris.
sentences.ko: 다음 목요일 이른 아침, 너는 용감하고 고귀한 젊은 패리스 백작과 결혼한다.

sentences.en: The wedding will be at Saint Peter's Church.
sentences.ko: 성 베드로 성당에서 말이야.

sentences.en: He will make you a happy bride there.
sentences.ko: 그곳에서 그는 너를 행복한 신부로 만들어 줄 거다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Now by Saint Peter’s Church, and Peter too,
He shall not make me there a joyful bride.
I wonder at this haste, that I must wed
Ere he that should be husband comes to woo.
I pray you tell my lord and father, madam,
I will not marry yet; and when I do, I swear
It shall be Romeo, whom you know I hate,
Rather than Paris. These are news indeed.

sentences.en: I swear by Saint Peter's Church and by Saint Peter himself.
sentences.ko: 성 베드로 성당과 성 베드로를 걸고 맹세해요.

sentences.en: He will not make me a happy bride.
sentences.ko: 그는 저를 행복한 신부로 만들어 주지 못할 거예요.

sentences.en: I am surprised by this hurry.
sentences.ko: 이렇게 서두르는 게 놀라워요.

sentences.en: I must marry before the man who should be my husband can try to win my love.
sentences.ko: 신랑이 될 사람이 구애하기도 전에 결혼해야 한다니요.

sentences.en: Please tell my father, madam.
sentences.ko: 어머니, 아버지께 전해 주세요.

sentences.en: I will not marry yet.
sentences.ko: 아직 결혼하지 않을 거예요.

sentences.en: When I do marry, I promise it will be Romeo.
sentences.ko: 결혼하게 되면, 맹세코 로미오와 할 거예요.

sentences.en: You know that I hate him.
sentences.ko: 제가 그를 증오한다는 걸 아시잖아요.

sentences.en: I would rather marry him than Paris.
sentences.ko: 패리스보다 차라리 그와 결혼하고 싶어요.

sentences.en: That is news for you!
sentences.ko: 정말 놀라운 소식이죠!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Here comes your father, tell him so yourself,
And see how he will take it at your hands.

sentences.en: Your father is coming here.
sentences.ko: 네 아버님이 오신다.

sentences.en: Tell him the truth yourself.
sentences.ko: 직접 진실을 말해라.

sentences.en: See how he reacts to your words.
sentences.ko: 네 말에 그분이 어떻게 반응하시는지 봐라.

raw: Enter Capulet and Nurse.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
When the sun sets, the air doth drizzle dew;
But for the sunset of my brother’s son
It rains downright.
How now? A conduit, girl? What, still in tears?
Evermore showering? In one little body
Thou counterfeits a bark, a sea, a wind.
For still thy eyes, which I may call the sea,
Do ebb and flow with tears; the bark thy body is,
Sailing in this salt flood, the winds, thy sighs,
Who raging with thy tears and they with them,
Without a sudden calm will overset
Thy tempest-tossed body. How now, wife?
Have you deliver’d to her our decree?

sentences.en: When the sun sets, the air produces dew.
sentences.ko: 해가 지면 공기 중에 이슬이 맺힌다.

sentences.en: But for the sunset of my brother's son, it rains heavily.
sentences.ko: 하지만 조카의 해가 저무니 비가 억수로 쏟아지는구나.

sentences.en: What is it, girl? Are you a fountain?
sentences.ko: 웬일이냐, 얘야? 분수라도 된 거냐?

sentences.en: Are you still crying and always crying?
sentences.ko: 왜 계속 울고 또 우는 것이냐?

sentences.en: In your small body, you act like a boat, a sea, and a wind.
sentences.ko: 작은 몸으로 배와 바다, 그리고 바람이 되어버렸구나.

sentences.en: Your eyes are like the sea because they flow with tears.
sentences.ko: 눈물이 흐르니 네 눈은 마치 바다 같구나.

sentences.en: Your body is like a boat sailing in this salty flood of tears.
sentences.ko: 네 몸은 이 짠 눈물의 파도 속을 항해하는 배와 같다.

sentences.en: Your sighs are like the winds that rage together with your tears.
sentences.ko: 너의 한숨은 눈물과 함께 몰아치는 바람과도 같구나.

sentences.en: Without a sudden calm, the storm will sink your body.
sentences.ko: 갑작스러운 평온이 오지 않으면 폭풍이 네 몸을 가라앉힐 것이다.

sentences.en: What is it, wife? Have you told her our decision?
sentences.ko: 여보, 어떻게 됐소? 우리 결정을 그 애에게 전했소?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Ay, sir; but she will none, she gives you thanks.
I would the fool were married to her grave.

sentences.en: Yes, sir, but she refuses, thank you very much.
sentences.ko: 네, 그런데 싫답니다. 고맙다면서요.

sentences.en: I wish the fool were married to her grave.
sentences.ko: 저 바보는 차라리 무덤과 결혼하면 좋겠어요.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Soft. Take me with you, take me with you, wife.
How, will she none? Doth she not give us thanks?
Is she not proud? Doth she not count her blest,
Unworthy as she is, that we have wrought
So worthy a gentleman to be her bridegroom?

sentences.en: Wait, explain that to me, wife.
sentences.ko: 잠깐, 무슨 말인지 똑똑히 말해 보시오, 부인.

sentences.en: What, she refuses?
sentences.ko: 뭐라고, 아이가 거절했다고?

sentences.en: Does she not thank us or feel proud?
sentences.ko: 고마운 줄도 모르고, 자랑스럽지도 않단 말이오?

sentences.en: Does she not feel lucky, unworthy as she is, that we found such a worthy gentleman for her?
sentences.ko: 보잘것없는 주제에, 우리가 그렇게 훌륭한 신사를 구해 준 걸 복으로 여기지도 않는단 말이오?

speaker: JULIET

sentences.en: I am not proud that you have found him, but I am thankful that you tried.
sentences.ko: 그분을 찾아 주신 걸 자랑스럽게 여기지는 않지만, 애써 주신 건 감사해요.

sentences.en: I can never be proud of what I hate.
sentences.ko: 제가 싫어하는 일에 대해서는 결코 자부심을 느낄 수 없어요.

sentences.en: But I am thankful even for hate that is meant as love.
sentences.ko: 하지만 사랑으로 여겨지는 증오조차도 저는 감사하게 생각해요.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
How now, how now, chopp’d logic? What is this?
Proud, and, I thank you, and I thank you not;
And yet not proud. Mistress minion you,
Thank me no thankings, nor proud me no prouds,
But fettle your fine joints ’gainst Thursday next
To go with Paris to Saint Peter’s Church,
Or I will drag thee on a hurdle thither.
Out, you green-sickness carrion! Out, you baggage!
You tallow-face!

sentences.en: What is this?
sentences.ko: 이게 무슨 소리냐?

sentences.en: This logic is confusing.
sentences.ko: 논리가 엉망이구나.

sentences.en: You are proud, and you thank me, and you do not thank me.
sentences.ko: 자부심을 느끼면서 고마워하면서, 동시에 고마워하지 않는다고?

sentences.en: And yet you are not proud.
sentences.ko: 그러면서 자부심도 없다고?

sentences.en: You spoiled little madam!
sentences.ko: 이 건방진 계집아이!

sentences.en: Don't 'thank' me, and don't 'proud' me.
sentences.ko: 고맙다는 말도, 자부심이라는 말도 집어치워라.

sentences.en: Get your fine body ready for next Thursday.
sentences.ko: 다음 주 목요일을 위해 몸단장을 해라.

sentences.en: Go with Paris to Saint Peter's Church.
sentences.ko: 패리스와 함께 성 피터 성당으로 가거라.

sentences.en: Or I will drag you there on a prisoner's cart.
sentences.ko: 안 그러면 죄수 호송 수레에 실어서라도 끌고 가겠다.

sentences.en: Get out, you pale, sick piece of rotten meat!
sentences.ko: 나가라, 이 창백하고 병든 고기 덩어리 같은 년아!

sentences.en: Get out, you worthless girl!
sentences.ko: 쓸모없는 계집애야, 당장 나가라!

sentences.en: You candle-faced thing!
sentences.ko: 양초처럼 허연 얼굴 같으니!

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Fie, fie! What, are you mad?

sentences.en: Stop, stop!
sentences.ko: 그만하세요, 그만요!

sentences.en: Are you mad?
sentences.ko: 제정신이세요?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Good father, I beseech you on my knees,
Hear me with patience but to speak a word.

sentences.en: Good father, I beg you on my knees.
sentences.ko: 아버지, 무릎을 꿇고 간청드려요.

sentences.en: Listen to me patiently.
sentences.ko: 제 말을 차분히 들어보세요.

sentences.en: Let me speak just one word.
sentences.ko: 한 마디만 말하게 해주세요.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Hang thee young baggage, disobedient wretch!
I tell thee what,—get thee to church a Thursday,
Or never after look me in the face.
Speak not, reply not, do not answer me.
My fingers itch. Wife, we scarce thought us blest
That God had lent us but this only child;
But now I see this one is one too much,
And that we have a curse in having her.
Out on her, hilding.

sentences.en: Hang you, you disobedient girl!
sentences.ko: 목이나 매라, 이 불효막심한 계집애야!

sentences.en: I tell you what: go to church this Thursday or never look at my face again.
sentences.ko: 잘 들어라, 이번 주 목요일에 교회에 가지 않으면 내 얼굴을 다시는 보지 못할 줄 알아라.

sentences.en: Do not speak, reply, or answer me.
sentences.ko: 말도 하지 말고 대답도 하지 마라.

sentences.en: My fingers itch.
sentences.ko: 손이 근질거리는구나.

sentences.en: Wife, we felt unlucky that God gave us only one child.
sentences.ko: 부인, 하나님이 자식을 하나밖에 안 주셨다고 우린 서운해했지.

sentences.en: But now I see she is too much for us.
sentences.ko: 그런데 이제 보니 그 하나도 너무 많군.

sentences.en: Having her is a curse. Curse her, the worthless girl!
sentences.ko: 이 애를 둔 게 저주야. 이 쓸모없는 것!

speaker: NURSE
raw:
God in heaven bless her.
You are to blame, my lord, to rate her so.

sentences.en: May God in heaven bless her.
sentences.ko: 하늘의 신께서 아이를 축복하시길 빌어요.

sentences.en: You are to blame, my lord, for speaking to her so harshly.
sentences.ko: 주인님, 아가씨를 그렇게 꾸짖으시다니 잘못하신 거예요.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
And why, my lady wisdom? Hold your tongue,
Good prudence; smatter with your gossips, go.

sentences.en: And why, my lady wisdom?
sentences.ko: 왜, 잘난 지혜 부인?

sentences.en: Hold your tongue, Miss Know-it-all, and go chatter with your gossip friends.
sentences.ko: 입 좀 다물고, 아는 체하는 여인아, 가서 네 수다쟁이 친구들과 떠들어라.

speaker: NURSE
raw: I speak no treason.

sentences.en: I am not saying anything wrong.
sentences.ko: 저는 틀린 말을 하는 게 아니에요.

speaker: CAPULET
raw: O God ye good-en!

sentences.en: Oh, for God's sake, go away!
sentences.ko: 세상에, 제발 좀 저리 가!

speaker: NURSE
raw: May not one speak?

sentences.en: May I not speak?
sentences.ko: 제가 말도 못 하나요?

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
Peace, you mumbling fool!
Utter your gravity o’er a gossip’s bowl,
For here we need it not.

sentences.en: Be quiet, you foolish person!
sentences.ko: 조용히 해, 이 중얼대는 멍청이야!

sentences.en: Save your wise words for your gossip friends over a drink.
sentences.ko: 그 똑똑한 소리는 술이나 마시며 네 수다쟁이 친구들과나 나누라고.

sentences.en: We do not need them here.
sentences.ko: 여기선 필요 없으니까.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: You are too hot.

sentences.en: You are being too angry.
sentences.ko: 너무 흥분하셨어요.

speaker: CAPULET
raw:
God’s bread, it makes me mad!
Day, night, hour, ride, time, work, play,
Alone, in company, still my care hath been
To have her match’d, and having now provided
A gentleman of noble parentage,
Of fair demesnes, youthful, and nobly allied,
Stuff’d, as they say, with honourable parts,
Proportion’d as one’s thought would wish a man,
And then to have a wretched puling fool,
A whining mammet, in her fortune’s tender,
To answer, ‘I’ll not wed, I cannot love,
I am too young, I pray you pardon me.’
But, and you will not wed, I’ll pardon you.
Graze where you will, you shall not house with me.
Look to’t, think on’t, I do not use to jest.
Thursday is near; lay hand on heart, advise.
And you be mine, I’ll give you to my friend;
And you be not, hang, beg, starve, die in the streets,
For by my soul, I’ll ne’er acknowledge thee,
Nor what is mine shall never do thee good.
Trust to’t, bethink you, I’ll not be forsworn.

sentences.en: Oh, this makes me mad!
sentences.ko: 제기랄, 미치겠구나!

sentences.en: Day and night, working or playing, alone or with others, I have had one concern.
sentences.ko: 낮이나 밤이나, 일할 때나 놀 때나, 혼자일 때나 여럿과 있을 때나, 내 머릿속엔 한 가지 생각뿐이었다.

sentences.en: I wanted to find her a husband.
sentences.ko: 그 애에게 남편을 찾아 주는 것이었지.

sentences.en: I have now found a gentleman of noble parents.
sentences.ko: 이제 고귀한 가문 출신의 신사를 찾았다.

sentences.en: He has fine lands, he is young, and he is from a noble family.
sentences.ko: 그는 좋은 땅도 있고 젊으며, 명망 있는 집안 출신이다.

sentences.en: He has many honorable qualities.
sentences.ko: 그는 훌륭한 자질을 많이 갖추고 있다.

sentences.en: He is exactly the kind of man I wanted.
sentences.ko: 그는 내가 원하던 바로 그런 남자다.

sentences.en: And then to have a foolish girl crying like a baby.
sentences.ko: 그런데 이 바보 같은 계집애가 아기처럼 울어대다니.

sentences.en: She is a whining puppet who says no when good luck is offered.
sentences.ko: 복이 굴러왔는데 싫다고 칭얼대는 꼭두각시 같으니.

sentences.en: She says, 'I will not marry, I cannot love.'
sentences.ko: 그 애는 '결혼 안 할 거야, 사랑할 수 없어'라고 말한다.

sentences.en: She says, 'I am too young, please forgive me.'
sentences.ko: 그 애는 '난 너무 어려요, 용서해 주세요'라고 말한다.

sentences.en: But if you will not marry, I will 'forgive' you all right.
sentences.ko: 하지만 네가 결혼을 거부한다면, 내가 기꺼이 '용서'해주마.

sentences.en: Go where you want, but you will not live with me.
sentences.ko: 어디서든 풀이나 뜯어 먹어라. 이 집에서 살 생각은 마라.

sentences.en: Think about it. I am not joking.
sentences.ko: 생각해 봐라. 농담이 아니다.

sentences.en: Thursday is near. Put your hand on your heart and decide.
sentences.ko: 목요일이 코앞이다. 네 가슴에 손을 얹고 결정해라.

sentences.en: If you are mine, I will give you to my friend.
sentences.ko: 네가 내 딸이라면, 내 친구에게 시집보내겠다.

sentences.en: If you are not mine, hang, beg, starve, or die in the streets.
sentences.ko: 내 딸이 아니라면, 목을 매든 빌어먹든 굶든 길거리에서 죽든 마음대로 해라.

sentences.en: I swear by my soul that I will never acknowledge you.
sentences.ko: 내 영혼을 걸고 맹세컨대, 난 너를 절대 인정하지 않을 것이다.

sentences.en: Nothing of mine will ever help you.
sentences.ko: 내 것 중 그 무엇도 네게 도움이 되지 않을 것이다.

sentences.en: Trust me. Think about it. I will not break my promise.
sentences.ko: 내 말을 믿어라. 잘 생각해 봐라. 내 약속은 어기지 않을 테니.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Is there no pity sitting in the clouds,
That sees into the bottom of my grief?
O sweet my mother, cast me not away,
Delay this marriage for a month, a week,
Or, if you do not, make the bridal bed
In that dim monument where Tybalt lies.

sentences.en: Is there no pity in the clouds?
sentences.ko: 구름 위에는 제 슬픔의 밑바닥까지 보시는 자비도 없나요?

sentences.en: Does anyone see how sad I am?
sentences.ko: 제가 얼마나 슬픈지 아무도 모르시나요?

sentences.en: Oh sweet mother, do not cast me away.
sentences.ko: 오, 어머니, 저를 버리지 마세요.

sentences.en: Delay this marriage for a month or a week.
sentences.ko: 이 결혼을 한 달이나 일주일만 미뤄주세요.

sentences.en: Or, if you do not, make my wedding bed in that dark family tomb where Tybalt lies.
sentences.ko: 아니면, 그러지 않으시겠다면, 티볼트가 누워 있는 그 어두운 가문의 무덤에 제 결혼 침대를 마련해 주세요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Talk not to me, for I’ll not speak a word.
Do as thou wilt, for I have done with thee.

sentences.en: Do not talk to me. I will not say a word.
sentences.ko: 나한테 말하지 마라. 한마디도 안 할 테니.

sentences.en: Do what you want. I am finished with you.
sentences.ko: 네 멋대로 해라. 너와는 끝이다.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O God! O Nurse, how shall this be prevented?
My husband is on earth, my faith in heaven.
How shall that faith return again to earth,
Unless that husband send it me from heaven
By leaving earth? Comfort me, counsel me.
Alack, alack, that heaven should practise stratagems
Upon so soft a subject as myself.
What say’st thou? Hast thou not a word of joy?
Some comfort, Nurse.

sentences.en: Oh God! Oh Nurse, how can we stop this?
sentences.ko: 오, 신이시여! 유모, 우리가 어떻게 이걸 막을 수 있겠어?

sentences.en: My husband is on earth, and my faith is in heaven.
sentences.ko: 내 남편은 지상에 있고, 내 믿음은 하늘에 있어.

sentences.en: How can I take back that vow?
sentences.ko: 그 맹세를 어떻게 되돌릴 수 있겠어?

sentences.en: Only if my husband dies and sends it back to me from heaven.
sentences.ko: 남편이 죽어서 하늘에서 돌려보내 주지 않는 한.

sentences.en: Comfort me. Give me advice.
sentences.ko: 나를 위로해 줘. 조언을 해줘.

sentences.en: Oh no, that heaven should use tricks on a person as gentle as myself.
sentences.ko: 아, 하늘이 나같이 여린 사람에게 이런 계략을 쓰다니.

sentences.en: What do you say?
sentences.ko: 어떻게 생각해?

sentences.en: Do you not have a word of joy?
sentences.ko: 기쁜 말 한마디 없어?

sentences.en: Give me some comfort, Nurse.
sentences.ko: 위로 좀 해줘, 유모.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Faith, here it is.
Romeo is banished; and all the world to nothing
That he dares ne’er come back to challenge you.
Or if he do, it needs must be by stealth.
Then, since the case so stands as now it doth,
I think it best you married with the County.
O, he’s a lovely gentleman.
Romeo’s a dishclout to him. An eagle, madam,
Hath not so green, so quick, so fair an eye
As Paris hath. Beshrew my very heart,
I think you are happy in this second match,
For it excels your first: or if it did not,
Your first is dead, or ’twere as good he were,
As living here and you no use of him.

sentences.en: Well, here it is.
sentences.ko: 자, 여기 상황이 이래.

sentences.en: Romeo is banished.
sentences.ko: 로미오는 추방당했어.

sentences.en: I would bet the whole world that he will never dare come back to claim you.
sentences.ko: 그가 너를 차지하러 감히 돌아올 일은 절대 없을 거라고 내 모든 걸 걸고 장담해.

sentences.en: Or if he does, it must be in secret.
sentences.ko: 설령 온다 해도 비밀리에 올 거야.

sentences.en: Since things are as they are, I think it is best that you marry the Count.
sentences.ko: 상황이 이렇게 됐으니, 백작과 결혼하는 게 최선이야.

sentences.en: He is a lovely gentleman.
sentences.ko: 그는 아주 멋진 신사야.

sentences.en: Romeo is a dirty rag next to him.
sentences.ko: 로미오는 그 사람에 비하면 걸레야.

sentences.en: An eagle does not have such green, quick, and beautiful eyes as Paris has.
sentences.ko: 독수리도 패리스처럼 초록빛의 생기 넘치고 아름다운 눈을 가질 순 없어.

sentences.en: Upon my heart, I think you will be happy in this second marriage.
sentences.ko: 내 진심으로 말하는데, 너는 두 번째 결혼에서 행복할 거야.

sentences.en: It is better than your first one.
sentences.ko: 첫 번째보다 훨씬 나을 거야.

sentences.en: If it is not, your first husband is dead.
sentences.ko: 그렇지 않더라도 네 첫 남편은 이미 죽은 거나 다름없어.

sentences.en: Or he is as good as dead, since he lives far away and is no use to you.
sentences.ko: 멀리 살고 있어서 아무 소용도 없으니 사실상 죽은 거나 마찬가지니까.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Speakest thou from thy heart?

sentences.en: Do you speak from your heart?
sentences.ko: 진심으로 하는 말이야?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
And from my soul too,
Or else beshrew them both.

sentences.en: And I speak from my soul.
sentences.ko: 내 영혼을 걸고 하는 말이야.

sentences.en: Otherwise, may they both be cursed.
sentences.ko: 안 그러면 둘 다 저주를 받아도 좋아.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Amen.

sentences.en: Amen.
sentences.ko: 아멘.

speaker: NURSE
raw: What?

sentences.en: What?
sentences.ko: 뭐?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Well, thou hast comforted me marvellous much.
Go in, and tell my lady I am gone,
Having displeas’d my father, to Lawrence’ cell,
To make confession and to be absolv’d.

sentences.en: Well, you have comforted me very much.
sentences.ko: 그래, 덕분에 마음이 훨씬 편해졌어.

sentences.en: Go in and tell my lady that I am gone.
sentences.ko: 들어가서 어머니께 내가 나갔다고 전해 줘.

sentences.en: I have upset my father.
sentences.ko: 아버지 마음을 상하게 해 드렸으니

sentences.en: I am going to Lawrence's cell.
sentences.ko: 로런스 신부님의 수도실에 가서

sentences.en: I must go to confess and be forgiven.
sentences.ko: 고해하고 용서를 받을 거야.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Marry, I will; and this is wisely done.

sentences.en: Of course I will.
sentences.ko: 그럼, 그래야지.

sentences.en: This is a wise thing to do.
sentences.ko: 그건 현명한 생각이야.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Ancient damnation! O most wicked fiend!
Is it more sin to wish me thus forsworn,
Or to dispraise my lord with that same tongue
Which she hath prais’d him with above compare
So many thousand times? Go, counsellor.
Thou and my bosom henceforth shall be twain.
I’ll to the Friar to know his remedy.
If all else fail, myself have power to die.

sentences.en: Damned old woman!
sentences.ko: 망할 늙은이!

sentences.en: Oh, you wicked fiend!
sentences.ko: 오, 이 사악한 악마!

sentences.en: Is it a worse sin to want me to break my marriage vow?
sentences.ko: 내 결혼 맹세를 깨라고 하는 게 더 큰 죄일까?

sentences.en: Or to insult my husband with the same tongue that praised him thousands of times?
sentences.ko: 아니면 수천 번이나 칭찬하던 그 혀로 내 남편을 헐뜯는 게 더 큰 죄일까?

sentences.en: Go, adviser.
sentences.ko: 가라, 조언자여.

sentences.en: I will never share my secrets with you again.
sentences.ko: 이제 내 속마음은 다시는 너와 나누지 않겠다.

sentences.en: I will go to the Friar to find his remedy.
sentences.ko: 신부님께 가서 방법을 여쭤봐야겠다.

sentences.en: If everything else fails, I have the power to die.
sentences.ko: 모든 게 실패해도, 나에겐 죽을 힘이 있다.

raw: Exit.
